text: The raw table is filling continuously now, but nothing knows which rows are new since the last check. This video builds the mechanism that tracks exactly that: a Snowflake Stream.

A stream isn't a copy of the data -- it's an offset into the table's own change history. Querying it returns metadata columns like METADATA$ACTION and METADATA$ISUPDATE, flagging exactly what kind of change each row represents.
We create the stream on POS_TRANSACTIONS_RAW and query it directly. Since Pinehurst's POS data is insert-only, every pending row shows up as a plain INSERT, never an update.
One detail matters more than it looks: the stream's offset only advances when a consuming statement actually commits. A rolled-back read leaves every pending row exactly where it was.
That's not a side note -- it's what makes the next video's scheduled merge safe to retry if it ever fails partway through.
